messages:
alex: handing off evening shift — quick consolidated handoff for the group (root msg ts 1849990000)

alex: TL;DR: multi-region embedding throttles earlier today (eu-west primary), brief 503s for ~18m affecting a subset of premium customers; autoscaler config and routing oddities traced. No data loss.

alex: timeline in brief:
- 18:03 UTC incident-bot: page triggered, high 5xx rate on embeddings-east/west.
- 18:05 sam: confirmed spike, started containment (regional scale-down to force fallback).
- 18:12 maria: identified autoscaler overshoot + HPA pod churn during burst.
- 18:21 lee: applied temp routing rule to route traffic to dedicated embedding pool for premium customers.
- 18:25 issue subsided; monitoring showed p95 restored by 18:31.

maria: root cause summary: autoscaler interacted poorly with recent kube node drain behaviour under burst traffic + a KV cache missstorm. Autoscaler scaled up but probes failed, which caused a small window where routing saw no healthy pods and tripped 503s.

sam: customer impact: about ~1200 requests (~0.03% of daily embed volume) saw 503s; affected customers were largely on dedicated plans hitting large batched embedding requests. Notified CCR; CS already sent initial outreach.

lee: mitigation actions taken during shift:
- temporarily pinned premium routes to dedicated pool (route-id: premium-eu-dedicated).
- increased probe timeout on embed service to 12s (was 3s) to avoid flapping on cold starts.
- adjusted HPA thresholds to be less aggressive for burst windows.

nora: followups / next steps (actionable):
1) Create small canary to test probe-timeout change across canary pool before wider rollout — owner: maria (ETA: 24h).
2) Add kube drain / autoscaler interaction note to runbook and link preflight check — owner: lee (ETA: 48h).
3) Run replay of burst traffic in staging with KV cache cold state to validate HPA behaviour — owner: sam (ETA: 72h).
4) Post-incident review doc and customer impact spreadsheet — owner: alex (ETA: 48h).

alex: runbook pointers and links:
- playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embed-throttle
- autoscaler troubleshooting doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/hpa-troubleshoot
- quick commands used during triage:
```
# check pods in eu-west
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=embed-service -o wide
# view HPA status
kubectl -n inference get hpa embed-hpa -o yaml
# tail logs
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=embed-service --since=30m
```

incident-bot: Pager summary: pages: embeddings-5xx (sev-2) at 18:03, resolved 18:31, total duration 28m (mitigation window ~18m).

oncall-bot: Handoff checklist check: primary: alex (evening), secondary: maria. Shadow: n/a for tonight. Coverage gap: none critical but monitoring for auto-scaler regressions overnight.

maria: note for overnight oncall: watch for repeat 5xx spikes and for increased pod restart counts (kubectl get pods -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount). If you see sustained restart growth + HPA scale events, escalate to eng-runtime pager (pager:eng-runtime).

sam: I'd add to that: if premium route continues to see errors after our mitigations, flip premium-eu-dedicated back to global fallback (route set: prefer-dedicated=false) to spread load; ping me and lee before doing global fallback.

lee: handoff notes to oncoming shift: no config pushes planned tonight. If you need to rollback probe-timeout change, revert config map embedded-probe-timeout in infra-configs and restart embed pods in canary only.

alex: final status: incident resolved, current state: premium routing pinned to dedicated pool, monitoring OK, post-incident actions assigned. Next update: I will post the PIR draft to #postmortems tomorrow AM after collecting logs.

nora: quick ack: thanks team. I'm taking primary on the followups with alex as secondary for the PIR.

alex: end of handoff — ping me if anything flares. :thumbsup:
